draft.emotion: warm and glowing, smiling with quiet satisfaction
notes: Commonly followed by the prepositions 'akan', 'atas', or (in everyday speech) 'dengan' or 'sama' to introduce what one is proud of.
Always positive in meaning. For negative pride ('arrogant', 'stuck-up'), use 'sombong' or 'angkuh'.

senses.definition: Feeling happy and satisfied about something you or someone close to you has achieved.

examples.text: Saya sangat bangga dengan prestasi anak saya di sekolah.
examples.translation: I am very proud of my child's achievement at school.
examples.emotion: warm and beaming, speaking with deep parental affection

draftBefore.emotion: warm and glowing, smiling with quiet satisfaction
notes: Bangga has two very different sides: feeling good about an achievement (proud), and thinking too highly of oneself (arrogant or boastful). Context will tell you which one is meant.
Do not confuse bangga with sombong. While bangga can mean arrogant in a negative way, sombong is the standard and much more common word for someone who is stuck-up and looks down on others.

senses.definition: Feeling happy and satisfied about something you or someone else has achieved.

examples.text: Saya sangat bangga dengan prestasi anak saya di sekolah.
examples.translation: I am very proud of my child's achievement at school.
examples.emotion: warm and beaming, speaking with deep parental affection

senses.definition: Having an excessively high opinion of oneself; arrogant or boastful.

examples.text: Jangan menjadi orang yang bangga dan suka meremehkan orang lain.
examples.translation: Do not be an arrogant person who likes to look down on others.
examples.emotion: stern and warning, shaking a finger in gentle admonishment

faults.quote: Having an excessively high opinion of oneself; arrogant or boastful.
faults.why: Bangga is positive ('proud'); it does not mean 'arrogant' (which is 'sombong' or 'angkuh').

faults.quote: thinking too highly of oneself (arrogant or boastful)
faults.why: False claim; bangga does not mean arrogant unless used in rare phrases like 'bangga diri'.
